expansion_contract.fact_row: verified official-source, canonical-state, workflow-evidence or acceptance-contract fact
expansion_contract.boundary_row: prevents checker predictions, address-base gaps, provider omissions, operational orderability limits, take-up rates or future deployment plans from being promoted to exact current postcode or parcel coverage without accepted r2 bytes and hardened postjoin evidence

source_routes.name: Ofcom broadband checker – about and FAQs
Ofcom broadband availability checker results semantics
About this data – fixed coverage and full-fibre take-up (v2)
Canonical slot state and current source probe

facts.detail: The checker uses Ordnance Survey property data and updates its base dataset twice a year, so newly created or changed properties may not appear immediately.
A missing postcode or address in the checker is not evidence that broadband is unavailable at that property.

guard_streams.write_limit: Address-dataset lag must not be converted into a parcel no-coverage result.

facts.detail: The coverage checker does not report maintenance or current service outages; users are directed to provider status information.
Published availability is not a live operational-health measurement.

guard_streams.write_limit: Do not label a current outage, restoration state or uptime from coverage records.

facts.detail: The checker classifies standard broadband as a predicted download speed below 30 Mbit/s.
The checker groups superfast as 30–300 Mbit/s and ultrafast as above 300 Mbit/s.

guard_streams.write_limit: Category bands are predicted availability classes, not observed parcel throughput.

facts.detail: FWA coverage information is based on operators’ predictive modelling tools.
Local conditions may prevent a particular premises receiving service even where FWA is predicted.

guard_streams.write_limit: A predicted FWA result cannot be promoted as confirmed installation or measured speed.

facts.detail: If no speed prediction is shown, Ofcom states this does not necessarily mean broadband is unavailable.
The checker directs users to network-provider availability pages when predictions are absent.

guard_streams.write_limit: Unknown checker output remains NO_DATA or review; it is not a negative candidate.

facts.detail: Checker information is collected from broadband network providers.
Ofcom notes that some networks, particularly smaller providers, may not yet be included.

guard_streams.write_limit: Provider omission risk prevents treating a red or empty result as universal market absence.

facts.detail: A service shown as available may still be unavailable at a specific location or time for operational reasons.
Property access, landlord permission, equipment maintenance or upgrades may affect actual orderability.

guard_streams.write_limit: Checker availability must not be represented as a guaranteed ready-to-install service.

facts.detail: Received speed can differ from predictions because of in-building networking and simultaneous device use.
Line length, age and repair condition can also affect actual performance.

guard_streams.write_limit: Do not convert maximum predicted availability into measured end-user performance.

facts.detail: Displayed download and upload values are the highest predicted speeds supplied by relevant network operators.
The checker explicitly warns that actual property availability and received speeds may differ.

guard_streams.write_limit: The web layer must label these values as predictions and area/address availability, never measurements.

facts.detail: A green tick means generally available in the area, while amber means available to some but not all properties.
A red cross represents the checker’s category-level not-available result.

guard_streams.write_limit: Area icons cannot independently establish a canonical parcel identity or exact provider orderability.

facts.detail: Ofcom states that the January 2026 data collected for Connected Nations was used to update its broadband and mobile checkers.
The relevant fixed broadband availability evidence remains a January 2026 snapshot rather than a continuously observed feed.

guard_streams.write_limit: Snapshot freshness must be retained explicitly in every candidate record.

facts.detail: Headline full-fibre and gigabit-capable coverage figures focus on residential premises.
Full-fibre take-up and premises without decent broadband are reported across residential and commercial premises.

guard_streams.write_limit: Residential headline percentages cannot be applied to the all-premises parcel shard.

guard_streams.source: Ofcom fixed coverage data dictionary v2

facts.detail: The data provides take-up as a share of full-fibre-covered premises and separately as a share of all premises in a local authority.
Take-up percentage can fall while active connections rise when coverage expands faster, and adoption may lag awareness or contract expiry.

guard_streams.write_limit: Local-authority take-up is contextual evidence and cannot populate postcode coverage or parcel speed.

facts.detail: The planned-deployment report covers operators’ stated fixed and FWA build plans through the end of 2028.
Ofcom states that plans can change and the published figures are not comprehensive or definitive.

guard_streams.write_limit: Future build forecasts must remain separate from current January 2026 availability.

facts.detail: Ofcom does not intend to put confidential future-build information into the broadband checker.
The checker is intended to update after providers report properties covered or ready for service.

guard_streams.write_limit: A planned network footprint cannot promote a parcel candidate until current ready-for-service evidence exists.
